children: opened a new Thai manufacturing facility on Thursday, deepening its presence in Southeast Asia as Thailand rolls out a long-term strategy to build a broader semiconductor industry.

The Samut Prakan facility near Bangkok will handle advanced power modules, wafer testing, and research and development, serving demand from electric vehicles, energy storage, clean energy, and advanced electronics.

The company opened the facility near Bangkok on Thursday, with an initial investment of more than €100M ($114M). The project is part of a 48B baht ($1.4B) investment in Thailand, according to the country's Board of Investment.
The first module has up to 30,000 square meters of cleanroom space, with the site designed to expand to 150,000 square meters across five modules.

Infineon COO Alexander Gorski said Thailand could eventually move into semiconductor production, although wafer fabrication is unlikely within the next three years. He pointed to the country's logistics, semiconductor supply chain, and geopolitical neutrality as factors supporting its longer-term potential.
“Bangkok is more than a manufacturing hub for Infineon; it helps strengthen the diversification of our strategic long-term investment,” Infineon COO Alexander Gorski said.
Thailand on Thursday approved its first national semiconductor and advanced electronics strategy, targeting $80B in cumulative investment and more than 230,000 jobs by 2050.
The BOI said Thailand received applications for 879 semiconductor and advanced electronics projects worth $27.2B from 2023 through H1 2026.

title: Infineon opens new Thailand manufacturing plant in $1.4B expansion
